card.summary: No free tier published. The home page sells seedbox and VPS hosting in the Netherlands with "10Gbps Unlimited traffic" and "50+ apps One-click install".

free_tier.stated: No free tier published. The home page sells seedbox and VPS hosting in the Netherlands with "10Gbps Unlimited traffic" and "50+ apps One-click install".
free_tier.notes: the price is not on the home page

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: a rented seedbox, so the plan disk is the only object store and no per-file cap is published

retention.stated: not applicable: the volume is rented for the plan term

egress.terms: Unlimited traffic, stated on the home page as "10Gbps Unlimited traffic". No byte allowance is published.

record.interface_detail: the home page names one-click applications, not retrieval protocols
record.tooling: vendor lists 50+ one-click apps including Plex, Jellyfin, Emby, Sonarr, Radarr and SABnzbd
record.chaining: a rented seedbox gives a retrieval endpoint with no client hardware; it composes with a debrid key or a public index, and the client retrieves over whatever protocol the plan exposes
record.limits_note: no named constraint was read: the home page publishes throughput and no byte cap

identity_cost.detail: a client area is required to deploy; the signup fields were not read

record.reliability_note: site answered 200 on 2026-10-23 after the record had called it dead on the evidence of a JS configurator and two 404 paths
record.confidence_note: the vendor page was read; the price, the cap and the retrieval protocol were not

evidence.proved: HTTP 200; "10Gbps Unlimited traffic", "50+ apps One-click install", "NL hosted Netherlands datacenter", and the application list

record.notes: Corrected from verdict dead to paid-only on 2026-10-23: the pricing paths 404 but the service sells hosting and answers. The earlier rejection was a read failure, not a dead provider.

dead_end.why: Pricing is behind a JS configurator; /seedbox-plans/ and /seedbox-hosting/ both 404, homepage returns a heading with no plan table. Third-party figures ($25/3TB = $8.33/TB) are…

record.binding_note: nothing in the vocabulary was found to fail at this scale; the offer is a paid plan and its disk size is the only stated limit
